The correct answer is 'DBCA'.

Key Points

  • 'Lakua and his wife' mentioned in sentence B refer to the phrase 'a poor couple' in sentence D. Hence, 'B' follows 'D'.

  • The adverb 'finally' indicates that 'A' is the last sentence.
     

Important Points

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the paragraph and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences of the paragraph (concluding sentence).

Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

B. The father went to the roadside and shouted, “John!”

C. No one answered.

D. They looked in the garden, and did not find him there.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ADBC'.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting off a story, starting of an incident or an event, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
  • Sentence A will be the starting line because it contains the main idea of the para jumble i.e. the tailor and his wife discovering that their son was not in the house.
  • However, Sentence D states that they looked in the garden, and did not find him there. So, D will follow A.
  • Further, Sentence B states that the father after looking in the garden went to the roadside and shouted, “John!” & Sentence C states that no one answered. So, C will follow B.
  • Thus, the correct sequence is:
    • A: One day the tailor and his wife discovered that their son was not in the house.
    • D: They looked in the garden, and did not find him there.
    • B: The father went to the roadside and shouted, “John!”
    • C: No one answered.
       

Correct Sequence: One day the tailor and his wife discovered that their son was not in the house. They looked in the garden, and did not find him there. The father went to the roadside and shouted, “John!” No one answered.

D. The Curies had to work in extreme poverty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is DACB

Key Points

When we combine the sentences to form a paragraph, it is important to establish a connection between them.

  • A sentence cannot start with words like - thus, generally, hence. They are concluding words, which denotes end of the idea. Thus B is ruled out.
  • A sentence cannot start with a conjunction in the beginning. It must have a reference to the subject or the idea in the previous sentence. Thus sentence C cannot form the beginning of the sentence.
    Eg: *But in the West, people have jobs.
  • The subject of the paragraph is clearly mentioned in sentence D. The curies had to work in extreme poverty.
  • A is followed after D. It shows a connection with the word 'even'. It tells that  Even the most ill-equipped laboratory would have been better than their shed.
  • A contradiction is showed by the conjunction 'but' which is in line C. It states that the mind of the curies was set upon the discovery of radium.
  • Finally, the conclusion is drawn by line B. It gives information that they did not allow any difficulties in their way.

Thus the correct order is DACB.

The Curies had to work in extreme poverty. Even the most ill-equipped laboratory would have been better than their shed. But their mind was set upon the discovery of radium. Thus, they did not allow any difficulties to come in their way.

When other options are used to frame the sentences, it does not fit structurally. There is no proper connection between them.
